newsitem.title: USA: TCI Communications splits up cable systems.
newsitem.headline: TCI Communications splits up cable systems.

text.p: TCI Communications Inc said Wednesday that its cable operations will be organized into three separate groups, a new structure it said would better allow it to focus on "the differing individual needs of each system group."
Group A will consist of a large group of cable systems in various urban and metropolitan markets that are preparing to offer new services on advanced cable systems.
Group B will consist of cable systems where TCI's digital television product, ALL TV, can be deployed.

Group C will consist of systems in Hartford, Conn., Chicago suburbs, and parts of the San Francisco Bay area in which the company previously announced its intention to offer integrated delivery of its core cable product, ALL TV, the wireline telephone service known as People Link, and its Internet service known as @Home.
Barry Marshall, the executive vice president of TCI's cable operations, has been named president of Group A.
Marvin Jones, formerly with Liberty Media and United Artists cable, has been named president of Group B.
Barbara Mowry, senior vice president of TCI's customer service division, has been named president of Group C.

"This new organization will help us deploy ALL TV faster," TCI President and Chief Executive Brendan Clouston said in a statement. "It also will help us devise winning competitive strategies for categories of systems that have common business, regulatory and operating environments."
Other management and organizational changes related to the announcement are to be announced shortly, the company said.
